elisa.title: Why are ELISA tests important for animal health?
elisa.subtitle: ELISA supports preventive medicine and evidence-based herd management.

early_diagnosis.label: 🧪 Early diagnosis
early_diagnosis.content: Some infectious diseases can be detected through laboratory testing before clinical signs are fully developed. This allows timely action to prevent disease spread within the farm.

herd_monitoring.label: 🐄 Herd health monitoring
herd_monitoring.content: ELISA results help evaluate the spread of diseases on the farm and monitor the overall immunological status of the herd.

vaccination_assessment.label: 💉 Evaluation of vaccination programs
vaccination_assessment.content: Monitoring antibody levels for specific diseases can be used to evaluate vaccination program effectiveness. The results provide veterinarians with additional data for better vaccination strategy planning.

epidemiological_surveillance.label: 🦠 Epidemiological surveillance of infections
epidemiological_surveillance.content: ELISA tests are an important diagnostic tool for investigating infectious disease spread on farms, assessing risks, and designing disease control programs.

poultry_importance.label: 🐔 Special importance in poultry
poultry_importance.content: In poultry farms, ELISA testing enables systematic monitoring of flock health status. Serological monitoring can be carried out for Newcastle disease, infectious bronchitis, Gumboro disease, and other major infections.
